notes: Use Uber/Ola (air-conditioned) and black-and-yellow taxis (metered); suburban trains are very crowded (the first carriage is reserved for women). Metro Line 3 (Colaba-Bandra-airport) has been running since 2025. The airport takes 45-90 minutes depending on traffic.
The best time is November to February (25-30°C, dry). March to May is 35°C and humid. Diwali falls in October and the Ganesh festival in September (statues are immersed at Chowpatty).
Get an e-Visa (30 days) online. Carry cash in INR (break your 500 notes); UPI is limited for foreigners, and cards work at larger places.
Street food: vada pav 20-30, pav bhaji 100, bhel puri 60; breakfast at an Irani cafe 300; restaurant meals 600-1,000. Drink bottled water; be careful with ice and raw salads.
Elephanta is closed on Mondays and Britannia on Sundays; go to Haji Ali at low tide; museums open at 10:15.
Take the Dharavi tour only with a responsible company (Reality Tours); a Bollywood studio tour (Film City) costs 2,000+ INR.

stops.name: Gateway of India
stops.tips: A basalt triumphal arch built in 1924, opposite the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel. Watch the morning pigeons and boats.

stops.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
stops.tips: The former Prince of Wales Museum: an Indo-Saracenic dome, miniature paintings and an audio guide.

stops.name: Kala Ghoda Art District
stops.tips: Galleries, the free Jehangir Art Gallery and Rhythm House; there is a festival in February.

stops.name: Leopold Cafe
stops.tips: A Parsi cafe dating from 1871 (of Shantaram fame); beer and chicken tikka, with bullet marks still on the walls.

stops.name: Colaba Causeway
stops.tips: A street market: haggle, and clothes and souvenirs are cheap.

backups.name: Bademiya Colaba
backups.tips: A late-night kebab stand behind the Taj: seekh kebab and roti.

backups.name: Afghan Church Colaba
backups.tips: A church from 1858; quieter than Kala Ghoda.

stops.name: Elephanta Caves
stops.tips: 1 hour by ferry from the Gateway (about 200 INR, first boat 09:00); 6th-century rock-cut Shiva temples, the Trimurti and 120 steps. Watch out for monkeys; closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Gateway of India Ferry Terminal
stops.tips: For the return trip; Elephanta has only snacks.

stops.name: Britannia & Co Ballard Estate
stops.tips: A Parsi cafe from 1923; berry pulao, closed on Sundays and shuts at 16:00.

stops.name: Marine Drive
stops.tips: The "Queen's Necklace", a 3.6 km seafront; walk from Nariman Point to Chowpatty and watch the sunset and the street lamps.

stops.name: Girgaon Chowpatty Beach
stops.tips: The beach has bhel puri and pav bhaji stands; swimming is not allowed.

backups.name: Kanheri Caves Sanjay Gandhi
backups.tips: If the ferry is cancelled: 109 Buddhist caves in the national park, near Borivali.

backups.name: Cafe Mondegar Colaba
backups.tips: A cafe with Mario Miranda murals; beer and sandwiches.

stops.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic station with 3 million passengers a day. Look from outside and in the hall.

stops.name: Dhobi Ghat Mahalaxmi
stops.tips: The world's largest open-air laundry; view it from the bridge, or take a tour for 200 INR.

stops.name: Haji Ali Dargah
stops.tips: A shrine in the sea dating from 1431; reached by a causeway (open only at low tide), with loudspeaker chanting. A head covering is required.

stops.name: Haji Ali Juice Centre
stops.tips: The famous juice shop opposite; try the custard apple cream.

stops.name: Mani Bhavan Gandhi Museum
stops.tips: Gandhi's Mumbai home between 1917 and 1934; in Gamdevi, free entry.

backups.name: Shree Thaker Bhojanalay Kalbadevi
backups.tips: Unlimited Gujarati thali; a well-known spot.

backups.name: Mahalaxmi Temple
backups.tips: A seaside temple; go here instead of Haji Ali at high tide.

stops.name: Dharavi Slum Tour Reality Tours
stops.tips: One of Asia's largest slums, with recycling, leather and pottery workshops. Go with a responsible tour; no photos are allowed, and 80% of the income goes to the community.

stops.name: Mahim Dargah
stops.tips: A 15th-century shrine near Dharavi.

stops.name: Sarvi Byculla
stops.tips: A place from the 1920s; seekh kebab and khichda; in Byculla.

stops.name: Banganga Tank
stops.tips: A sacred tank on Malabar Hill dating from 1127; a village-like corner of Mumbai.

stops.name: Hanging Gardens Malabar Hill
stops.tips: Sculpted hedges and views of Marine Drive; the Shoe House is in Kamala Nehru Park.

backups.name: Bhau Daji Lad Museum Byculla
backups.tips: The city's oldest museum; in Byculla, as an alternative to Banganga.

backups.name: Swati Snacks Tardeo
backups.tips: A Gujarati street food restaurant; panki and dahi puri.

stops.name: Mount Mary Basilica
stops.tips: A basilica on Bandra Hill; the Bandra Fair takes place in September.

stops.name: Bandstand Promenade
stops.tips: The seafront; Shah Rukh Khan's home Mannat, and views of the Sea Link from Bandra Fort.

stops.name: Candies Bandra
stops.tips: A cafe with a garden; Parsi and Goan food, a city favourite.

stops.name: Linking Road and Hill Road
stops.tips: A street market selling cheap shoes and clothes.

stops.name: Carter Road Sunset
stops.tips: A rocky seafront promenade; popular with Bandra's young crowd, with cafes.

backups.name: Elco Bandra
backups.tips: A pani puri and chaat stop on Hill Road.

backups.name: Pali Village Cafe
backups.tips: An ivy-covered cafe in Pali Hill; go in the evening.

stops.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
stops.tips: A 100 km² forest inside the city, at Borivali. There are leopards (not seen in daytime) and a tiger safari.

stops.name: Kanheri Caves
stops.tips: 109 Buddhist caves dating from the 1st century BCE to the 10th century; 20 minutes by park bus.

stops.name: Global Vipassana Pagoda
stops.tips: The world's largest stone dome, in Gorai; take the ferry (from Borivali West). Meditation is offered.

stops.name: Juhu Beach
stops.tips: The Bollywood beach: pav bhaji and gola stands, and sunset; swimming is not allowed.

stops.name: Prithvi Cafe Juhu
stops.tips: A theatre cafe; Irish coffee and keema pav, with play evenings.

backups.name: Anand Stall Juhu
backups.tips: Vada pav and dosa opposite Mithibai College; street food.

backups.name: ISKCON Juhu
backups.tips: The Hare Krishna Temple; a nearby alternative to the pagoda.

days.theme: Fort morning and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Asiatic Society Library Town Hall
stops.tips: A neoclassical building from 1830 on Horniman Circle; its steps look like a Bollywood set.

stops.name: Horniman Circle Gardens
stops.tips: A garden and St Thomas Cathedral (1718).

stops.name: Kyani & Co Marine Lines
stops.tips: An Irani cafe from 1904; bun maska and chai, keema; a farewell stop.

stops.name: Ashok Vada Pav Dadar
stops.tips: The city's most famous vada pav (potato fritter in a bread roll); near Kirti College.

stops.name: Mumbai Airport Metro/Taxi
stops.tips: 45-90 minutes by Uber/Ola, depending on traffic; farewell.

backups.name: Yazdani Bakery Fort
backups.tips: An Irani bakery from 1953; brun maska.

backups.name: Flora Fountain
backups.tips: A fountain on Fort Square; an alternative to the garden.
